title: "Attention Is All You Need" and the Transformer Breakthrough (2017)
explainer: In June 2017, researchers at Google Brain and Google Research published "Attention Is All You Need," introducing the Transformer architecture, which dropped the recurrent and convolutional layers earlier neural networks relied on in favor of a self-attention mechanism that could be trained in parallel across an entire sequence. That shift toward massive parallelizability, more than any single new idea about "intelligence," is what let models scale up into the large language systems in use today. Reading how modestly the original paper frames its own contribution is a useful corrective to how dramatically "AI breakthroughs" tend to get mythologized after the fact.

title: The Perceptron and the First AI Winter
explainer: Frank Rosenblatt's Perceptron, demonstrated in 1958, was covered in the press with predictions that machines would soon walk, talk, and think, but Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert's 1969 book Perceptrons exposed sharp mathematical limits on what a single-layer network could learn, and funding for neural-network research dried up for years afterward in what is now called an AI winter. The cycle of inflated promises followed by a funding collapse recurred again in the 1980s, and recognizing that pattern is useful context for judging how durable any current wave of AI hype is likely to be.
